Quick update to the group and for the record (short):
- I applied a targeted rollback of the failover rule that inadvertently matched a broader prefix for eu-west workloads.
- Canary traffic (5% of EU requests) shows p95 reduced from ~420ms to ~140ms, p99 reduced from ~980ms to ~270ms.
- No impact on error rate. No config drift detected in other regions.
- I’ve pushed the full rollback to all gateways; propagation ongoing (expected 6–12 minutes).

Attaching an incident timeline and the diff we used for the rollback. I’ll stay on the bridge until propagation completes.

Rishi
Senior SRE

From: jonas.weber@redwood.ai
To: Sven Larsson <sven.larsson@acme-corp.com>, tessa.morgan@redwood.ai, rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai, dev_patel@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 26 Feb 2026 19:47:00 -0800
Subject: RESOLVED: EU p95/p99 regressions — root cause and postmortem plan

Sven / Acme team — thanks again for patience and for surfacing this quickly. Final summary below: 

What happened:
- During a planned resilience rollout (02/24), a failover route-policy was applied with an overly broad CIDR match that caused a subset of EU traffic to be routed to US-west gateways. Increased RTT resulted in sharp p95/p99 regressions for synchronous API calls.

Impact:
- p95 for EU dropped from ~420ms to ~140ms after rollback; p99 from ~980ms to ~270ms.
- Affected ~11% of EU requests (impact window ~21:40–22:10 UTC on 02/24).

What we did:
- Identified and rolled back the offending route-policy in canary, validated latency improvements, then rolled out the full rollback across gateways (propagation complete).
- No customer data leaked, error rates unchanged.
- Created INF-1245 and scheduled a blameless postmortem.

Next steps / ask from Acme (we will):
- Share detailed timeline and tracing slices (done; link below).
- Offer a credit for the incident window as per our SLA — I’ll coordinate with finance.
- Propose a follow-up meeting to review resilience rollout checklist and regional routing validation tests.

Links & artifacts:
- Incident ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-1245
- Traces & dashboards: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1Xr-example-incident-doc
- Attachments: p95_spike_eu_to_us-west.png; incident_timeline.xlsx; routing_policy_diff.patch

If this summary looks good, Tessa and I will schedule a 30-min review with your platform/infra team tomorrow.

— Jonas
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
